box.name: box
box.description: Pads its content on all sides, with an optional border and an optional surface.

attributes.name: data-gap
attributes.description: Padding on every side.

attributes.name: data-gap-inline
attributes.description: Padding on the two sides only, over whatever data-gap set: a band wide at the sides and ordinary top and bottom.

attributes.name: data-gap-block
attributes.description: Padding top and bottom only, over whatever data-gap set.

attributes.name: data-surface
attributes.description: Fill the box with one of the three surface tones, making it a visible panel. Absent, the box is transparent and only its padding does anything.

markers.name: data-border
markers.description: Draw a border of the border width, in the border color. Works on any element; it is a box's most common marker, which is why it is listed here.

markers.name: data-paint
markers.description: Fill this element with a color by name: a hue at its base step with the text made for it, a constant, or a step of the greyscale. Up to grey-40 the text stays the page text; from grey-50 it becomes the page surface.

markers.name: data-text
markers.description: Color this element's words by name, from the same list. On an element that is also painted it wins over the automatic text color.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-md
tokens.description: The default padding.

tokens.name: --yeti-color-surface
tokens.description: The fill at data-surface="base"; the page's own surface.

tokens.name: --yeti-color-surface-raised
tokens.description: The fill at data-surface="raised", a step above the page.

tokens.name: --yeti-color-surface-sunken
tokens.description: The fill at data-surface="sunken", a step below the page.

a11y.notes: Purely visual. A box has no semantics; use a section or article element when the content is one.

breakout.name: breakout
breakout.description: Keeps its children in a centered reading column with gutters, and lets any child carrying data-bleed span the full width.

attributes.name: data-max
attributes.description: The widest the reading column may be.

attributes.name: data-gap
attributes.description: The gutter on each side, and the space between children.

children.description: The content, in the column. Any child may carry data-bleed to span the full width.
Children that break out of the column.
A margin note: in the end gutter beside the child it follows when the breakout is wide, in the column when it is not.

markers.name: data-bleed
markers.description: Breaks the child out of the column to span the full width.

markers.name: data-note
markers.description: A margin note: in the end gutter beside the child it follows when the breakout is wide, in the column when it is not.

tokens.name: --yeti-width-md
tokens.description: The default column width, chosen under the base measure so paragraphs fill it.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-md
tokens.description: The default gutter and row gap.

tokens.name: --yeti-heading-space-before
tokens.description: The space above a heading, counted from what comes before it.

tokens.name: --yeti-heading-space-after
tokens.description: The space between a heading and what it opens.

tokens.name: --yeti-text-sm
tokens.description: The note's text size.

tokens.name: --yeti-color-text-muted
tokens.description: The note's text color.

a11y.notes: Purely visual. A bleeding child is still in reading order.

center.name: center
center.description: Centers a column of content horizontally, up to a maximum width, with gutters on narrow screens.

attributes.name: data-max
attributes.description: The widest the content column may be.

attributes.name: data-gap
attributes.description: The gutter on each side when the container is narrower than the maximum.

attributes.name: data-intrinsic
attributes.description: Shrink the column to its content (still no wider than data-max) and center it, with each child centered on its own width inside it.

tokens.name: --yeti-width-xl
tokens.description: The default maximum.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-md
tokens.description: The default gutter.

a11y.notes: Purely visual.

cluster.name: cluster
cluster.description: Lays its children out in a row that wraps, keeping one gap between them on both axes.

attributes.name: data-gap
attributes.description: Space between items, horizontally and between wrapped rows.

attributes.name: data-align
attributes.description: Vertical alignment of items within a row.

attributes.name: data-justify
attributes.description: How items are distributed along the row.

attributes.name: data-threshold
attributes.description: The cluster's own width below which it is a column of full-width items; at or above it, the wrapping row. Makes the cluster a size container, so it takes the width of its block instead of its content.

children.description: Anything sized by its content: tags, buttons, links, a logo and a nav.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-md
tokens.description: The default gap.

a11y.notes: Purely visual. Use a list element when the items are a list.

columns.name: columns
columns.description: Lays its children out as equal columns when the container is wider than a threshold, and as rows when it is not.

attributes.name: data-threshold
attributes.description: The container width below which the columns become rows.

attributes.name: data-gap
attributes.description: Space between columns, and between rows once they stack.

attributes.name: data-align
attributes.description: Vertical alignment of the columns.

attributes.name: data-justify
attributes.description: Distribution of the columns along the row when they do not fill it.

attributes.name: data-columns
attributes.description: The most columns on one row; further children each take a full row.

children.description: The columns. Each gets an equal share of the row.
A child that takes several shares of the row: data-span="2" is twice a plain sibling. Below the threshold it stacks like the rest.

markers.name: data-span
markers.description: How many shares of the row the child takes: 2 is twice a plain sibling. Below the threshold it stacks like the rest.

tokens.name: --yeti-width-md
tokens.description: The default threshold.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-md
tokens.description: The default gap.

a11y.notes: Purely visual. Reading order is source order in both arrangements.

container.name: container
container.description: Makes its box the thing a container query measures, so what is inside can respond to its width instead of the viewport's.

children.description: Anything. The container itself arranges nothing.

markers.name: data-show
markers.description: Show this element only while the nearest size container is this wide or wider. Below that width it is not rendered at all, and it is not in the accessibility tree either.

markers.name: data-hide
markers.description: Hide this element once the nearest size container is this wide or wider. Below that width it is rendered as usual.

a11y.notes: Purely structural.

cover.name: cover
cover.description: Fills at least the viewport's height and centers one child vertically, with optional content pinned above and below it.

attributes.name: data-gap
attributes.description: Minimum space between the centered child and whatever sits above or below it.

attributes.name: data-height
attributes.description: The band's least height: a stop of the height scale, half the viewport, or the whole of it. Content taller than the band grows it; nothing is cut off.

children.description: A header, the centered child, a footer: any of them optional except the centered one.
Exactly one child carries data-center and is centered in the remaining space.

markers.name: data-center
markers.description: Centers the child in the space the others leave; exactly one child carries it.

tokens.name: --yeti-cover-height
tokens.description: The least height with no data-height, and at data-height="full".

tokens.name: --yeti-space-md
tokens.description: The default gap.

a11y.notes: Purely visual. Keep the page's h1 inside the cover when the cover is the hero.

frame.name: frame
frame.description: Holds one child in a fixed aspect ratio, cropping an image, video or embedded document to fill it and centering anything else.

attributes.name: data-ratio
attributes.description: Width to height.

children.description: One child: an image, video, picture, iframe, embed or object is stretched to fill and cropped; anything else is centered.

a11y.notes: Cropping hides parts of an image. Make sure the alt text describes what is visible, or use data-ratio to match the image so nothing is lost. An iframe needs a title saying what is in it, whatever shape it is cropped to.

grid.name: grid
grid.description: Fits as many equal columns as the container allows at a minimum width, up to an optional maximum count.

attributes.name: data-min
attributes.description: The narrowest a column may be. With none, only data-columns decides the count; none is meant to be paired with data-columns, and alone gives a single full-width column.

attributes.name: data-columns
attributes.description: The most columns allowed. Fewer appear when the container cannot fit that many at data-min; with data-min="none" the count is exact. With data-fold, the count only ever halves.

attributes.name: data-gap
attributes.description: Space between columns and rows.

attributes.name: data-rows
attributes.description: Line up the parts of the children across each row: the value is how many rows each child spans, one per part.

attributes.name: data-fold
attributes.description: Halve the column count as the grid narrows instead of stepping down one at a time. Needs data-columns 2, 4, or 6 and uses data-min as the width per column. data-min="none" has no meaning with a fold: the count needs a width per column.

attributes.name: data-tracks
attributes.description: A fixed number of equal tracks that children are placed on with data-start and data-span, leaving any track nothing is placed on empty. Replaces the fitted columns, so data-min and data-columns have no effect alongside it, and it does not mix with data-fold.

attributes.name: data-threshold
attributes.description: With data-tracks: the grid's own width below which every child takes the whole row, in source order; at or above it, the placement applies.

children.description: The cells. All are the same width, except in a tracks grid, where each covers the tracks it is placed on.

markers.name: data-start
markers.description: In a tracks grid, the column line the child begins on. Without it the child flows into the next free track.

markers.name: data-span
markers.description: In a tracks grid, how many tracks the child covers. Without it the child covers one.

tokens.name: --yeti-width-xs
tokens.description: The default minimum column width.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-md
tokens.description: The default gap.

a11y.notes: Purely visual. Use a list when the cells are a list of like things.

icon.name: icon
icon.description: Sizes an inline SVG to the surrounding text and aligns it with the text beside it.

attributes.name: data-gap
attributes.description: Space between the icon and its text.

attributes.name: data-align
attributes.description: How the icon lines up with the text: centered on the line, or on the baseline.

children.description: The icon, an inline SVG, sized to one em.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-xs
tokens.description: The default gap.

a11y.notes: When the icon sits beside text, give the SVG aria-hidden="true" so the text is the name. When it stands alone, give the SVG role="img" and an aria-label.

layer.name: layer
layer.description: Stacks its children in one box, later ones on top, with the box as tall as the tallest of them.

attributes.name: data-align
attributes.description: Vertical alignment of every child in the box. baseline behaves as start here.

children.description: The layers, bottom first.
A child that places itself vertically: start, center, end, stretch, or baseline.
A child that places itself horizontally: start, center, end, or stretch.

markers.name: data-align-self
markers.description: Where the child sits vertically: start, center, end, stretch, or baseline.

markers.name: data-justify-self
markers.description: Where the child sits horizontally: start, center, end, or stretch.

tokens.name: --yeti-color-scrim
tokens.description: Wash behind a figure's caption, so it reads over the picture.

tokens.name: --yeti-color-text
tokens.description: A figure caption over the picture, which is not the aside a caption under one is.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-xs
tokens.description: Block padding of that caption.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-sm
tokens.description: Inline padding of that caption.

a11y.notes: Everything stays in reading order. Text laid over a picture needs a contrast treatment (a scrim or a solid panel); the layer does not add one.

masonry.name: masonry
masonry.description: Packs items of uneven height into columns with no gaps under the short ones.

attributes.name: data-min
attributes.description: The narrowest a column may be. none is meant to be paired with data-columns, which then gives an exact count; alone it gives a single full-width column.

attributes.name: data-columns
attributes.description: The most columns allowed. Fewer appear when the container cannot fit that many at data-min.

attributes.name: data-gap
attributes.description: Space between columns and between items.

children.description: The items. Each keeps its own height.

tokens.name: --yeti-width-xs
tokens.description: The default minimum column width.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-md
tokens.description: The default gap.

a11y.notes: In browsers without native masonry, items read down each column and then across. Keep the source order meaningful on its own.

guarded: grid-template-rows: masonry (add a display: grid-lanes guard when its companion properties settle)

overlay.name: overlay
overlay.description: Holds one child over the rest, centered, without pushing anything around; the parent is the box it covers.

attributes.name: data-gap
attributes.description: The least space kept between the held child and the edges of the box.

attributes.name: data-fixed
attributes.description: Center the held child over the viewport instead of this box, and keep it there while the page scrolls.

children.description: The content underneath, in normal flow, and one held child.
Exactly one child carries data-over; it leaves the flow and is centered over the box.

markers.name: data-over
markers.description: Lifts the child out of the flow and centers it over the box; exactly one child carries it.

markers.name: data-fill
markers.description: On the same child: cover the box rather than sit centred in it, which is what a veil, a dimmer or a loading state wants. Positioning only, so a veil that wants its own content centred puts a layout inside itself.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-md
tokens.description: The default edge gap.

a11y.notes: Positioning only. The held child stays in reading order where it is in the source. A held child that interrupts the page needs focus management and a way to dismiss it, which the dialog and tooltip components provide; use those rather than this primitive alone for anything modal.

scroller.name: scroller
scroller.description: Lays its children out in a single row that scrolls horizontally.

attributes.name: data-gap
attributes.description: Space between items.

attributes.name: data-width
attributes.description: Give every item this width instead of its natural one.

attributes.name: data-snap
attributes.description: Snap each item's start edge into place as the track scrolls.

attributes.name: data-justify
attributes.description: Where each item settles along the track when data-snap is set: its start edge, its center, or its end. Nothing without data-snap.

children.description: The items. None shrinks; the track scrolls instead. A single wide item (a table, an image) is legal: the scroller then just gives that one item horizontal overflow.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-md
tokens.description: The default gap.

keyboard.action: Focuses the track so the arrow keys can scroll it.
Scroll the track.

a11y.notes: A scrollable region must be reachable from the keyboard: give it tabindex="0", role="region", and a name with aria-label.

sidebar.name: sidebar
sidebar.description: Places a fixed-width sidebar beside flexible content, and stacks them when the content would drop below half the width.

attributes.name: data-side
attributes.description: Which child is the sidebar: the first (start) or the last (end).

attributes.name: data-width
attributes.description: The sidebar's preferred width.

attributes.name: data-gap
attributes.description: Space between the two children, side by side or stacked.

attributes.name: data-align
attributes.description: Vertical alignment of the two children when side by side.

children.description: Exactly two: the sidebar and the content, in either order according to data-side.

markers.name: data-sticky
markers.description: Pins this child at --yeti-sticky-offset from the top of the scrollport while the other one scrolls past it. It takes its own height rather than the row's, since a stretched item has nowhere to move.

tokens.name: --yeti-width-sm
tokens.description: The default sidebar width.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-md
tokens.description: The default gap.

a11y.notes: Purely visual. Put the content first in the source when it matters more, and use data-side="end" to show the sidebar after it.

stack.name: stack
stack.description: Stacks its children vertically with one consistent gap between them.

attributes.name: data-gap
attributes.description: Space between children. A pair such as sm-lg grows fluidly from the first stop to the second.

attributes.name: data-align
attributes.description: Horizontal alignment of the children.

attributes.name: data-fill
attributes.description: Make the stack at least as tall as the viewport, so a child carrying data-split reaches the bottom.

attributes.name: data-rule
attributes.description: A line between children, of the border width in the border color, in the middle of each gap. The gap is unchanged.

children.description: Anything. Each child's margins are reset; the stack owns the space between them.
At most one child may carry data-split; it and everything after it are pushed to the end of the stack when the stack is taller than its content.

markers.name: data-split
markers.description: Pushes the child and everything after it to the end of the stack when the stack is taller than its content.

markers.name: data-space
markers.description: The gap before this one child, larger or smaller than the stack's own: more room above a heading, less between a label and its field. Does nothing on the first child; data-split wins on a child carrying both.

markers.name: data-sticky
markers.description: Pins this child at --yeti-sticky-offset from the top of the scrollport while the rest of the stack scrolls past it. It keeps the full width of the column, a stack stretching its children on the inline axis.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-md
tokens.description: The default gap.

tokens.name: --yeti-cover-height
tokens.description: The minimum block size when data-fill is set.

tokens.name: --yeti-border-width
tokens.description: Width of the data-rule line.

tokens.name: --yeti-color-border
tokens.description: Color of the data-rule line.

a11y.notes: Purely visual. Reading order is source order.

timeline.name: timeline
timeline.description: Lays its entries along a rail with a marker each, on one side, or on alternate sides of a centred rail when it is wide.

attributes.name: data-gap
attributes.description: Space between entries.

attributes.name: data-alternate
attributes.description: Put entries on alternate sides of a centred rail once the list is wide enough.

children.description: The entries, in order. Put a time, a heading, and text inside each.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-lg
tokens.description: The default gap, and the room between the rail and the entries.

tokens.name: --yeti-color-border-strong
tokens.description: The rail and the markers.

a11y.notes: Use an ordered list, so the sequence is announced, and a time element with datetime in each entry. The rail and markers are decorative. Give the ol role="list": removing the list markers removes the list semantics in some engines.

hero.name: hero
hero.description: Fills the viewport's height with copy on one side and a figure on the other, centered, and stacks them below a container width; the one-class form of a cover holding columns.

attributes.name: data-threshold
attributes.description: The container width below which copy and figure become rows.

attributes.name: data-gap
attributes.description: Space between copy and figure.

attributes.name: data-ratio
attributes.description: The figure's aspect ratio.

attributes.name: data-align
attributes.description: Vertical alignment of copy and figure when side by side.

attributes.name: data-side
attributes.description: Put the figure at the start or the end of the row regardless of source order. Once stacked, source order rules: write the copy first to meet the headline first on a phone. Moves it visually only; reading order stays as written.

attributes.name: data-height
attributes.description: The band's least height: a stop of the height scale, half the viewport, or the whole of it, as a cover takes it. Content taller than the band grows it.

children.description: Exactly two: the copy and the figure (an img, video, or picture, or an element wrapping one); the copy (the body) must not have an img, video, or picture as a direct child (it would be taken for a second figure). A figure with a figcaption keeps its caption below the picture.
A child that takes several shares of the row: data-span="3" beside a "2" is three fifths. Below the threshold both stack full width.

markers.name: data-min
markers.description: The narrowest this child may get while the two share a row; the other gives way. Stacked, it has no effect.

markers.name: data-span
markers.description: How many shares of the row this child takes; the other child's default is 1.

tokens.name: --yeti-cover-height
tokens.description: The least height with no data-height, and at data-height="full".

tokens.name: --yeti-width-lg
tokens.description: The default threshold.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-lg
tokens.description: The default gap.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-sm
tokens.description: The gap between the copy's children.

tokens.name: --yeti-text-sm
tokens.description: Text size of the caption.

tokens.name: --yeti-color-text-muted
tokens.description: The caption.

a11y.notes: When the hero is the page's opening, keep the h1 inside the copy and write the copy first: data-side changes where the figure sits in the row, not where it is read, and not the stacked order.

media.name: media
media.description: Puts a figure beside a block of text and stacks them when the text would drop below half the width; the one-class form of a sidebar holding a frame and a stack.

attributes.name: data-width
attributes.description: The figure's preferred width.

attributes.name: data-ratio
attributes.description: The figure's aspect ratio.

attributes.name: data-gap
attributes.description: Space between the figure and the text.

attributes.name: data-align
attributes.description: Vertical alignment of figure and text when side by side.

attributes.name: data-max
attributes.description: The widest the text may run side by side; the figure takes the rest of a wide row. data-width still sets where the two stack.

attributes.name: data-side
attributes.description: Put the figure at the start or the end while side by side, regardless of source order. Stacked, the source order holds.

children.description: Exactly two: the figure (an img, video, or picture, or an element wrapping one) and the body; the body must not have an img, video, or picture as a direct child (it would be taken for a second figure). A figure with a figcaption keeps its caption below the picture.

tokens.name: --yeti-width-xs
tokens.description: The default figure width.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-md
tokens.description: The default gap.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-sm
tokens.description: The gap between the body's children.

tokens.name: --yeti-text-sm
tokens.description: Text size of the caption.

tokens.name: --yeti-color-text-muted
tokens.description: The caption.

a11y.notes: The figure is cropped to its ratio, so alt text should describe what is visible. data-side changes where the figure sits, not where it is read.

shell.name: shell
shell.description: The page skeleton: header on top, footer at the bottom of the viewport when the page is short, and a body row where nav and aside sit beside main while there is room.

attributes.name: data-gap
attributes.description: Space between the rows, and between nav, main, and aside.

attributes.name: data-width
attributes.description: The preferred width of nav and aside. Three regions share a row once the container is about four times this width plus the gaps; two regions need about half that.

children.description: In order: an optional header, the body (a div holding nav, main, and aside, in that source order, or a bare main when there are no side regions), and an optional footer.
The body row. Its nav and aside take data-width; its main takes the rest and never drops below half.

markers.name: data-sticky
markers.description: Pins the nav or the aside at --yeti-sticky-offset from the top of the scrollport while main scrolls past it.

tokens.name: --yeti-cover-height
tokens.description: The shell's minimum block size; the viewport by default.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-md
tokens.description: The default gap.

tokens.name: --yeti-width-sm
tokens.description: The default nav and aside width.

a11y.notes: Meant for body or the page's outermost element. The landmarks do the work: one main; a label on nav when the page has more than one; aside for content that is complementary, not primary.

accordion.name: accordion
accordion.description: A column of disclosures built on details and summary, each opening to show its panel, with the browser doing the opening, the keyboard, and the announcing.

children.description: One disclosure each. Give them all the same name attribute to have the browser close the others when one opens.
The row that opens its panel; one per details, first inside it.

tokens.name: --yeti-accordion-border
tokens.description: The line between panels and around the set.

tokens.name: --yeti-accordion-padding
tokens.description: Padding of a summary and its panel.

tokens.name: --yeti-accordion-surface
tokens.description: Background of the set, and so of an open panel.

tokens.name: --yeti-accordion-summary
tokens.description: Background of a summary row, set apart from the panel below it.

tokens.name: --yeti-accordion-summary-hover
tokens.description: Background of a summary under the pointer.

tokens.name: --yeti-border-width
tokens.description: Width of those lines.

tokens.name: --yeti-radius-md
tokens.description: Corner of the set.

keyboard.action: Moves to the next summary.
Opens or closes the panel under the focused summary.

a11y.notes: This is native: details is a disclosure, summary is its button, and the open state is the open attribute, all announced without help. Put a heading inside the summary if the row is a section title, since summary is not a heading by itself. To open one at a time, give every details the same name attribute, which is the browser's own exclusive accordion; Yeti adds no attribute for it, because CSS cannot set one and script should not be needed.

unguarded: animating a grid row between 0fr and 1fr
discrete transition of content-visibility (where missing, the panel still grows open and shuts at once rather than shrinking)

affix.name: affix
affix.description: Joins a control with what belongs beside it, a unit, a symbol, a button, or another control, into one thing with a shared border and height.

children.description: The controls and their attachments, in visual order.
A control; every control grows to share the row.
A control; every control grows to share the row.
A text prefix or suffix.
A button prefix or suffix.

tokens.name: --yeti-control-radius
tokens.description: Outer corners.

tokens.name: --yeti-control-border
tokens.description: Border of the attachments.

tokens.name: --yeti-border-width
tokens.description: The width the members overlap by.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-sm
tokens.description: Inline padding of an attachment.

tokens.name: --yeti-text-md
tokens.description: Text size of an attachment.

tokens.name: --yeti-color-text-muted
tokens.description: Text of an attachment.

tokens.name: --yeti-color-surface-sunken
tokens.description: Background of an attachment.

a11y.notes: A prefix or suffix that carries meaning (a currency, a unit) must reach the control's accessible name or description: give the span an id and add it to the control's aria-describedby, or say it in the label. When the affix holds more than one control, the field's label names one of them and each other control needs its own aria-label. A button in the affix is an ordinary button. Usually the affix is the control slot of a field.

alert.name: alert
alert.description: A message in a hue: a tinted box with a colored edge, an optional icon, and an optional close button that the module wires up.

attributes.name: data-variant
attributes.description: Which hue: success for done, warning for careful, danger for wrong (alert is the same ladder under its Foundation 6 name), primary for news.

attributes.name: data-emphasis
attributes.description: How loud: medium is a tint, high a solid fill, low the border alone.

children.description: An icon, first, sized to the text.
A button, last, that removes the alert when alert.js is loaded.
The message, in any element.

markers.name: data-close
markers.description: The close button; removes the alert when alert.js is loaded.

tokens.name: --yeti-alert-radius
tokens.description: Corner radius.

tokens.name: --yeti-alert-padding
tokens.description: Padding inside.

tokens.name: --yeti-alert-edge
tokens.description: Width of the start edge, at every emphasis. Undeclared; falls back to four times the local --yeti-border-width.

tokens.name: --yeti-control-size
tokens.description: Size of the close button.

tokens.name: --yeti-border-width
tokens.description: The border on every side but the start edge.

tokens.name: --yeti-space-sm
tokens.description: Gap between the icon, the body, and the close button.

tokens.name: --yeti-color-text

a11y.notes: A lede takes no role and announces nothing of its own. It is ordinary prose set larger, and its position under the heading already says what it is.

lift.name: lift
lift.description: Raises the element slightly, or grows it a little, and deepens its shadow while the pointer is on it or a keyboard is inside it.

attributes.name: data-lift
attributes.description: Which gesture: rise by --yeti-lift-distance, or scale by --yeti-lift-scale, for a tile in a row where a rise would break the line.

tokens.name: --yeti-lift-ease
tokens.description: The curve the lift runs on.

tokens.name: --yeti-lift-duration
tokens.description: How long the lift takes; match a tinted hover to it.

tokens.name: --yeti-lift-distance
tokens.description: How far the element rises; reduced motion takes it to zero.

tokens.name: --yeti-lift-scale
tokens.description: How much the element grows at data-lift="scale"; reduced motion takes it to one.

tokens.name: --yeti-lift-shadow
tokens.description: The shadow the element casts once lifted.

a11y.notes: The lift answers :focus-visible on the element and on anything inside it, so a reader tabbing through a page of cards sees the same affordance a pointer gets. It is decoration on top of a focus ring, never a replacement for one; the ring comes from the reset and is untouched. Under reduced motion the element no longer moves and the deeper shadow carries the hover by itself.

print.name: print
print.description: Marks an element as belonging to one medium: on the printed page only, or on the screen only.

attributes.name: data-print
attributes.description: Which medium the element belongs to: only, on paper and nowhere else, or none, everywhere but paper.

a11y.notes: Both states are display: none in the medium they are not for, which takes the element out of the accessibility tree there as well. That is correct for this job and worth saying out loud: a paper-only line is not read out on screen, so it must never carry anything a reader on screen needs, and a screen-only control is not on the page a reader prints, so nothing on paper may depend on it. Text a screen reader should hear but nobody should see is visually-hidden, not this. A printed page is also a page with no color guarantee, so never let the print state be the only thing carrying a meaning.

visually-hidden.name: visually-hidden
visually-hidden.description: Takes words out of sight and leaves them in the accessibility tree, for the name a control needs when its face is a picture.

a11y.notes: This is the opposite of the hidden attribute, which removes the element from the accessibility tree as well: text carrying this class is still announced, in source order, and becomes part of the accessible name of whatever contains it. The two words in the name are there to keep the two apart. A control named twice is named once: where an aria-label is present the browser uses it and ignores the text inside, so use one or the other. Put only text in here. Anything focusable is still focusable and would take Tab focus with nothing on screen to show for it.
